rule: Entity platform turn-on methods must apply every optional kwarg the platform contract passes them (e.g. fan async_turn_on must apply percentage and preset_mode) rather than accepting and discarding them.
trigger: A platform entity method signature declares optional service kwargs such as percentage, preset_mode, brightness or transition, but the body never reads them.
rationale: Service calls silently lose user-supplied arguments: a turn_on with a percentage would leave the device at its previous speed, so the entity's advertised feature flags lie about what the service does.

evidence.excerpt: accepts `percentage` and `preset_mode` parameters but doesn't use them

rule: YAML configuration schemas must constrain enumerated options with vol.In over the known constants and normalize case with vol.Lower instead of accepting free-form cv.string when downstream code branches on specific values.
trigger: A voluptuous CONFIG_SCHEMA entry uses cv.string for a key whose value is later compared against named constants or treated specially by import/setup logic.
rationale: Unvalidated free-form YAML values reach import and setup code that assumes one of a fixed set, so a differently-cased or unknown value produces incorrect handling instead of a config validation error at load time.

evidence.excerpt: Please constrain this schema (e.g., vol.In([...]) and/or normalize to lowercase)

rule: Changes to config entry migration or import logic must ship migration tests covering the exact value shapes whose handling changed, including every stored location the value can come from.
trigger: A diff modifies async_migrate_entry, an import step, or normalization of stored config entry data, without adding test cases for the newly-handled input variants.
rationale: Existing migration tests exercise only one canonical value, so a case-normalization or extraction regression passes CI unnoticed and silently corrupts users' stored config entries on upgrade.

evidence.excerpt: Add migration coverage that asserts uppercase realms remain unchanged

rule: Platform entity classes must reuse the data attributes already stored by the integration's shared base entity in entity.py instead of re-assigning their own copy of the same object.
trigger: A platform module's __init__ assigns self.<something> to a constructor argument that it also passes to super().__init__, where the base entity in entity.py already stores it.
rationale: Duplicate references to the same coordinator data must be kept in sync by hand and diverge as the base entity evolves; the base entity is the single place the integration keeps device context.

evidence.excerpt: is redundant since the parent class `ProxmoxNodeEntity` already stores the node data

rule: EntityDescription subclasses must be named for the object they describe followed by the platform, matching the naming already used by the integration's other platform modules.
trigger: A new @dataclass EntityDescription subclass is added in a platform module with a name whose object/platform word order differs from the equivalent classes in the integration's sibling platforms.
rationale: Each integration carries one description class per object per platform; inconsistent word order makes the parallel platform files impossible to scan and invites referencing a class name that does not exist.

evidence.excerpt: It should be named `ProxmoxVMButtonEntityDescription` to be consistent with the binary_sensor platform's naming convention

rule: Config flow error translation must map only 4xx API failures to specific user-facing error keys; server-side (5xx) failures must be reported the same way the runtime setup path reports them.
trigger: A config_flow except branch converts a broad API exception into a specific abort/error key without inspecting the HTTP status code, while coordinator.py distinguishes client from server errors on the same endpoint.
rationale: A blanket translation shows the user a misleading cause ("no active nodes were found") for what the setup path already knows is a transient server error, sending them to fix the wrong thing.

evidence.excerpt: Translate only 4xx node-list failures to `no_nodes_found`

rule: Trigger async_start_reauth only for authentication failures (401); authorization or permission failures (403) must raise ConfigEntryError instead, since re-entering credentials cannot fix them.
trigger: A setup or coordinator except branch calls config_entry.async_start_reauth for any 4xx status, or for a generic API exception, without isolating 401.
rationale: Reauth on a 403 puts the user in a prompt loop re-entering credentials that were always correct; the actual fix is granting privileges, which only a ConfigEntryError message can communicate.

evidence.excerpt: narrowing reauth triggering to authentication failures only

rule: When a translated setup error interpolates an exception into translation_placeholders, the placeholder must carry the original library exception's detail (its message or __cause__), never the repr of a bare wrapper exception.
trigger: A ConfigEntryNotReady/ConfigEntryError raised with translation_placeholders formats an exception that was itself raised bare with `raise CustomError from err`.
rationale: The wrapper reprs as an empty class name, so the translated message that exists specifically to surface API error details shows the user nothing actionable.

evidence.excerpt: Consider either preserving the original exception message when raising `ProxmoxServerError`

rule: Dynamic entity add/remove logic must not treat a temporarily offline or unreachable device as removed; keep its last-known children or exclude it from the pruning step so entities are not re-added when it returns.
trigger: A coordinator update returns empty collections for a device based on an offline/unavailable status, and those collections feed a known-set intersection that drives async_add_entities.
rationale: Pruning on transient unavailability makes the same items look new on recovery, so async_add_entities attempts duplicate unique_ids, which Home Assistant logs as an error and ignores.

evidence.excerpt: Preserve prior VM/container discovery for offline nodes

rule: Changes to DeviceInfo fields such as configuration_url must be covered by snapshot tests of the device and entity registry for every device type the integration creates.
trigger: A diff adds or edits DeviceInfo attributes in an integration's entity.py without touching the snapshot tests or ambr snapshot files.
rationale: Device info is part of entity registration, and snapshot testing is how this repo pins registration output, so an untested configuration_url can silently regress for one device class while others still pass.

evidence.excerpt: snapshot testing would be an appropriate way to test this functionality

rule: Entity unique_id and DeviceInfo identifiers must include the parent object's identifier whenever a child resource name is only unique within its parent, so two parents exposing the same name do not collide.
trigger: A unique_id or DeviceInfo identifiers f-string is built from the config entry id plus a resource name, for a resource enumerated per node/hub/bridge rather than globally.
rationale: Names like `local` repeat across nodes, so without the parent identifier the second device collides with the first and its entities are dropped at registration.

evidence.excerpt: Include the node identifier in the storage DeviceInfo identifiers and entity unique_id

rule: Numeric sensor entity descriptions must declare a state_class consistent with the integration's sibling sensors of the same device_class so the sensor participates in long-term statistics.
trigger: A new SensorEntityDescription sets device_class and native_unit_of_measurement for a numeric value but omits state_class, while neighbouring descriptions in the same tuple set one.
rationale: Without a state_class the recorder keeps no long-term statistics for the sensor, so a capacity or total value silently behaves differently from every comparable sensor in the same integration.

evidence.excerpt: for the total storage sensor so it participates correctly in long-term statistics

rule: Uptime and other duration-since-boot sensors must not use SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT; omit state_class or use TOTAL, matching how existing core integrations model uptime.
trigger: A SensorEntityDescription combines SensorDeviceClass.DURATION or an uptime translation_key with state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT.
rationale: Uptime resets to zero on reboot, so MEASUREMENT statistics average a monotonically climbing value into meaningless long-term data; core precedent (UPnP, asuswrt) omits the class or uses TOTAL.

evidence.excerpt: other integrations typically omit `state_class` (e.g. UPnP) or use a cumulative class

rule: Raw unit strings taken from a device or API payload must be normalized and validated against Home Assistant's canonical units for the entity's device_class, falling back to the entity description's default when unrecognized, before being assigned to native_unit_of_measurement.
trigger: A payload or MQTT property value is assigned directly to self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement without mapping it through the canonical unit constants.
rationale: Payload units vary in capitalization, aliases and whitespace (`kwh` vs `kWh`), and a non-canonical unit breaks unit conversion and statistics for the whole entity.

evidence.excerpt: normalize and validate the unit before assigning it

rule: An EntityDescription must keep a single source of truth for the callable that produces an entity's value; do not add a factory field alongside a mandatory value_fn that it overrides.
trigger: A description dataclass gains an optional *_factory callable while the original mandatory callable field stays required, and the entity picks one at runtime.
rationale: Every description providing a factory must still supply a dead value_fn, so the two callables drift and readers cannot tell which one the entity actually uses.

evidence.excerpt: `value_fn_factory` makes `value_fn` effectively unused for any description that provides a factory

rule: When entity creation becomes conditional on optional payload keys, add a regression test using the reduced payload that asserts only the always-available entities are created and no KeyError occurs.
trigger: A platform's async_setup_entry gains `if "<key>" in data` guards around entity creation without a matching test fixture that omits those keys.
rationale: Reduced-permission or partial API responses are exactly the case the guard exists for; without a fixture exercising it, the reported KeyError can return unnoticed.

evidence.excerpt: Add a regression test using the reduced PVEVMUser node payload

rule: When value helpers return None so an entity reports `unknown` instead of becoming unavailable, add tests feeding payloads with the missing or None fields to prove the helpers return None without raising and the update does not crash.
trigger: New value_fn helpers introduce `return None` paths for absent payload fields, with tests covering only fully-populated and idle payloads.
rationale: The unknown-versus-unavailable distinction is the behaviour the change exists to produce, and an unguarded key lookup on a partial payload would raise inside the coordinator update rather than yielding unknown.

evidence.excerpt: Add a test case that exercises an active/non-idle job payload with missing/`None` fields

rule: A pull request must add only the entities and behaviour its title and description announce; extra platform entities must be removed or the PR description updated to cover them.
trigger: A platform module gains an additional entity description beyond the single feature named in the PR title/body.
rationale: New entities are user-visible additions reviewed and released against the PR description, so an unannounced one escapes review and misleads the changelog.

evidence.excerpt: Update the PR description (or remove the extra change)

rule: Do not commit developer-machine artefacts into an integration directory: local AI-assistant instruction files and absolute paths under a contributor's home directory must be removed or replaced with generic placeholders.
trigger: A new integration adds files such as CLAUDE.md, or any committed file containing absolute paths like /Users/<name>/ or C:\Users\<name>\.
rationale: These paths mean nothing to other contributors and the instruction file is personal tooling configuration, not part of the integration shipped to users.

evidence.excerpt: contains absolute local file system paths specific to the developer's machine

rule: Integration code may only call library APIs that exist in the exact version pinned in manifest.json requirements; bump the pinned requirement in the same PR when the code depends on a newer attribute or method.
trigger: A diff uses a client attribute or method while manifest.json requirements pin a version of that library that does not provide it.
rationale: The pinned version is what users install, so the mismatch surfaces as a setup failure (`object has no attribute ...`) that CI mocks hide but every real installation hits.

evidence.excerpt: this version of the client doesn't seem to have `is_connected`

rule: When service registration is moved into services.py, __init__.py must import async_setup_services and call it from an async_setup, and define CONFIG_SCHEMA = cv.config_entry_only_config_schema(DOMAIN).
trigger: A refactor adds services.py with async_setup_services while __init__.py loses its registration code and gains no async_setup that calls it.
rationale: Without the async_setup hook nothing imports services.py, so every service the integration used to expose silently disappears; existing integrations such as rainbird show the required shape.

evidence.excerpt: Register the services by adding an `async_setup` that calls `async_setup_services`
